Chapter 05

Signal in discarded barcodes: doublets, lost cells and empty droplets

18 records reviewed here, 29 records cited in the text

In this chapter

  1. Doublets as interactions
  2. Lost and damaged cells as a drug-response readout
  3. Empty droplets and hashtag negatives
  4. Risks
  5. Hypotheses worth testing in high-multiplex drug screens
  6. Records in this chapter

Standard QC throws away three kinds of barcode: doublets, damaged or low-RNA cells, and empty droplets, which include hashtag negatives. Each of them carries information. Four things are shown in published work:

  1. Some doublets are physically interacting cells (PMID 31237234). Doublet-based tools can recover contact networks from routine data (PMID 35536255, PMID 37638864).
  2. The number of cells recovered per hashed condition tracks drug toxicity (PMID 31806696).
  3. Empty droplets measure the ambient background well enough to clean protein data (PMID 35440536). In one pool, the ambient hashtag profile pointed to the most degraded sample (PMID 31266958).
  4. Common QC filters remove viable cells, including drug-resistant ones (PMID 40205439).

What has not been shown is whether these signals work as per-condition readouts in high-multiplex drug screens. We found no study that tests any of these against an orthogonal assay in that setting. In a screen with many conditions and few cells each, the barcodes that QC removes are not a fixed tax. How many there are, and of what kind, can differ by drug. That makes them a readout and a bias at the same time.

Doublets as interactions

Sorted pairs. PIC-seq sorts physically interacting cells and models each pair's transcriptome as a mixture of two singlet profiles. It found regulatory T cells to be the main T cell subtype interacting with dendritic cells in mouse lymph nodes (PMID 32152598). Another group applied the PIC-seq model to unsorted CITE-seq from 11 human kidney allograft biopsies (31,203 high-quality libraries). Three of six doublet clusters were called interacting complexes. Two of those occurred at 4.7 and 9.5 times the frequency expected for artefactual doublets, while two other clusters matched the expectation and were treated as artefacts (PMID 37638864). This is the clearest published use of an expected random-doublet rate as the test.

Mining routine data. Neighbor-seq trains a random forest on artificial multiplets, assigns every barcode a composition, and compares each cell-type pair's enrichment with re-simulated multiplets (100 by default). It recovered the microanatomy of small intestinal epithelium, terminal respiratory tract and splenic white pulp, and tumour topologies that agreed with spatial data (PMID 35536255). CIcADA calls doublets from multi-label cell-type scores. It keeps only clusters made entirely of observed doublets, then contrasts them with synthetic doublets of the same pair. In tumour datasets these doublets up-regulated immune-response genes (PMID 37745004). ULMnet reported the only head-to-head comparison, on FACS-sorted dendritic cell to T cell doublets with known partners. Sensitivity in vitro was 56% for ULMnet, 52.1% for Neighbor-seq and 21.7% for CIcADA. In vivo it was 39%, 29.2% and 15.1%. Precision was about 99% for ULMnet and Neighbor-seq (PMID 41583424). The ULMnet authors ran this comparison themselves.

Designs that keep pairs on purpose. ProximID, paired-cell sequencing and ClumpSeq sequence attached pairs or small clumps, and use one partner's identity or zonation to map interactions or place the partner in tissue space (PMID 29786092, PMID 30222169, PMID 34031373; Partial-dissociation sequencing).

Evidence that some doublets are biology. T cell to monocyte complexes can be isolated from human blood. They show polarised LFA1/ICAM1, and their frequency changes with infection and immunisation (PMID 31237234; t-cell-monocyte-complexes). Such complexes also sit inside the live-singlet gate, and one published "novel" mixed T and B population was likely made of them (PMID 32400942). A 2026 review names the main obstacle: there are no definitive markers that separate biological doublets from artefacts (PMID 42601345). In ovarian cancer, doublet-derived interaction networks were associated with response to therapy in cohorts of 7 and 13 patients (PMID 40280979, PMID 42511520). These are associations in small cohorts.

The random-doublet baseline. Random doublets follow Poisson loading. Their rate can be derived from mixing experiments even when cell types are mixed unequally (PMID 30202659). Hashing detects only cross-sample doublets, so it gives a lower bound. Even so, the 10x heuristic consistently fell below hashing-based rates, sometimes by more than twofold: 37% observed against 17% predicted in one mouse kidney dataset (PMID 41166377). If the expected rate is set too low, every abundant pair looks enriched. Neighbor-seq's null re-draws the observed cells and does not model loading (PMID 35536255).

Decomposing instead of discarding. DoubletDecon returns putative doublet clusters that have unique gene expression to the singlets. On mouse bone marrow its specificity rose from 80.7% to 95.0% with this rescue step (PMID 31693907). In an independent benchmark, however, it did not beat a library-size baseline, failed on four datasets and over-called doublets (PMID 33338399). DeepDoublet splits hepatocyte to endothelial doublets into their two transcriptomes (PMID 39695909). RCTD doublet mode fits one or two reference types per spatial pixel. On simulated doublets it called 81.1% correctly (PMID 33603203). Nobody has reported using it on droplet doublets (rctd-doublet-mode-droplets).

Lost and damaged cells as a drug-response readout

Counts. In sci-Plex, the number of cells recovered at each concentration gave a viability score that agreed with gold-standard measurements. 52 of 188 compounds (27%) cut viability by half or more at the top dose (PMID 31806696; Cell recovery per condition as a viability readout). Tahoe-100M reports quantifying proliferation and cytotoxicity across 50 cell lines and 1,100 drug-dose conditions (PMID 42753697; Tahoe-100M).

Survivors can look unchanged. MIX-Seq predicted long-term viability from transcriptional responses (one model across drugs, R2 0.50 at 24 h). The BCL-2 inhibitor navitoclax and the MCL1 inhibitor AZD5591 were the exceptions. Both had strong selective viability effects but no robust transcriptional signature (PMID 32855387; survivor-bias). For drugs like these, the effect lives in the cells that are gone. Drugs also change how much RNA a cell holds. Measured against spike-in molecules, paclitaxel or celecoxib alone generally repressed transcription per cell, while the combination amplified it (PMID 34159316). A count floor will therefore remove cells unevenly across treatments. This is an inference; the study did not test filtering.

Mitochondrial filters. Across 9 tumour datasets (441,445 cells, 134 patients), malignant cells had higher mitochondrial fractions without more dissociation stress. In 10 to 50% of tumour samples, cells above 15% mitochondrial reads were twice as common among malignant cells as in the microenvironment. In lineage-traced ovarian cancer clones, those resistant to olaparib or carboplatin had higher mitochondrial fractions than sensitive ones, rising further after treatment (PMID 40205439; mito-filter-resistant-cells). Adaptive thresholds are covered in miQC, ddqc and DropletQC.

Dead cells as a positive readout. Pooled CRISPR screens already sequence dead cells to turn negative selection into positive selection (PMID 37166646, PMID 37699398). MIX-Seq added floating cells back to the adherent fraction.

Composition. In a hashed pool, each condition's share of singlets is itself a composition, just like cell-type proportions. scCODA models counts against a reference category (mean MCC 0.64 in its own simulations, PMID 34824236). propeller (speckle) and Scanpro needs biological replicates (PMID 36005887). Its Python port Scanpro bootstraps pseudo-replicates, which by its authors' own account cannot reproduce biological variance (PMID 38971877). sccomp models mean-variability association and excludes outliers (PMID 37549298). A best-practice review notes that composition methods lack an independent benchmark heumos-2023. All of them test relative shares. A drug that kills every cell line equally leaves line shares unchanged, so absolute loss needs a denominator: vehicle wells, or spike-in reference cells. Cross-species reference cells have been used to measure per-sample contamination in drug-treated islets (PMID 32375897; Spike-in reference cells). Their use as a count denominator is untested.

Models that include loss. Waddington-OT estimates growth and death rates with unbalanced transport, using priors from proliferation and apoptosis signatures (PMID 30712874). moscot accepts growth and death rates as priors (PMID 39843746). CellOT maps control cells onto treated cells (PMID 37770709). Carrying a death term into drug-response models is proposed here, not published (unbalanced-ot-cell-loss).

Empty droplets and hashtag negatives

Empty droplets are already used as data. EmptyDrops tests barcodes against the ambient profile. In dsb, protein counts in empty droplets correlated with those of unstained spike-in cells, so they could serve as the background (PMID 35440536). demuxEM estimates background hashtags from empty droplets. In its brain-nuclei pool, one donor contributed disproportionately to that background. That donor had the lowest RNA integrity number and the longest post-mortem interval of the cohort (PMID 31266958). DecontPro found that some droplets called empty from their RNA held high tag counts, probably from neutrophils (PMID 37973397).

Ambient RNA carries its origin: in brain single-nucleus data it was mostly neuronal caglayan-2022. A toxicology review notes that chemical exposure kills cells and adds ambient RNA (PMID 38645720). In a pooled screen, however, the ambient RNA of all conditions mixes before encapsulation, so the RNA alone cannot say which condition lysed. souporcell estimates one ambient fraction for the whole pool, not one per source (PMID 32366989).

Risks

  • Random doublets read as interactions. Expected rates from loading heuristics are too low (PMID 41166377), and expression-based tools cannot see homotypic doublets.
  • Circularity. Doublets called from cell-type scores are then tested for enrichment of those same types. Synthetic doublets are built from the same data. Ambient RNA can push a singlet over a two-score threshold. QC thresholds fitted on the pooled data, then read back as a per-condition readout, measure the threshold as much as the drug.
  • Selection bias. Condition-dependent removal changes DE (survivors only), composition (relative shares) and pseudobulk weights at once (PMID 32855387, PMID 40205439). Outlier handling can drop the most cytotoxic well (sccomp).
  • Thin evidence. Most doublet tools are self-evaluated, with one external comparison on sorted pairs (PMID 41583424). The ambient-hashtag signal rests on one sample (PMID 31266958).

Hypotheses worth testing in high-multiplex drug screens

  1. An absolute denominator (Spike-in reference cells, unbalanced-ot-cell-loss). Test: add a fixed number of reference cells to every well. Check that the ratio of condition cells to reference cells matches viability, and compare DE results with and without a per-condition retained-fraction covariate.
  2. Doublet decomposition (rctd-doublet-mode-droplets). Test: run RCTD doublet mode on the public sorted DC-T doublet data used by ULMnet and compare sensitivity and precision with the published figures.

Whatever the readout, a screen should report, per condition, the barcodes assigned, the singlets kept, the barcodes removed by each filter, and the doublets by type. Without those numbers no one can tell drug effects from QC effects.

Chapter 11

Alignment, quantification, cell calling and ambient RNA

35 records reviewed here, 51 records cited in the text

In this chapter

  1. What the upstream choices do to the cells you keep
  2. Standard practice
  3. Benchmarked state of the art
  4. Published but not independently benchmarked
  5. Nuclei, intronic reads and multimapping: signal or artefact
  6. Hypotheses and open questions
  7. Recommendations for low-cell multiplexed drug screens
  8. Records in this chapter

Scope: the steps before any QC threshold is applied, namely how reads become a count matrix, how barcodes become cells, and how ambient RNA is measured and removed. The calling and QC review covers EmptyDrops, CB2, the first three ambient benchmarks and the four main ambient tools in depth (EmptyDrops, CB2, CellBender remove-background, SoupX, DecontX, scAR, janssen-2023, cargnelli-2026, nie-2026); this chapter adds the quantification layer, the other cell callers, the remaining ambient tools and two 2026 benchmarks, and does not repeat those numbers.

What the upstream choices do to the cells you keep

The count matrix is not a fixed input. Four choices made before QC change which barcodes look like cells and what they contain.

The quantifier. Independent comparisons agree on the direction of the differences. On three 10x datasets, kallisto reported the most cells, but the extra barcodes were low-gene and could not be labelled, and it detected Vmn and Olfr genes that are likely mapping artefacts; salmon alevin, using its own putative whitelist, found only about half of the cardiac endothelial cells that the other four tools found bruning-2022. On 22 public datasets from eight organisms, Cell Ranger called more cells than kallisto, but outside human and mouse the extras were low quality, while kallisto's higher gene detection revealed an extra photoreceptor type in zebrafish pineal gland shainer-2021. On mixtures with known labels, emptyDrops called about 60,000 cells on zUMIs and kallisto bustools output for a sample expected to hold about 3,000 you-2021. The quantifier and the caller interact: a caller tuned on one pipeline's UMI distribution does not transfer to another's.

Intronic reads. Counting reads in introns is now the default in Cell Ranger (from v7.0), and in nuclei it is necessary: exon-only references gave significantly smaller libraries and mislabelled astrocytes as neural stem cells in mouse cortex nuclei Counting intronic (nascent) reads, especially for nuclei. Turning it on shifts every barcode's UMI total, so a knee or a fixed UMI floor from an older run no longer selects the same barcodes.

The annotation. Using the unfiltered annotation (with pseudogenes and other biotypes) gave up to 10% more cells per sample and lower mito fractions bruning-2022. Poor 3' end annotation, intronic handling and overlapping genes each lose reads, and fixing the reference recovered missing marker genes and cell types Optimised transcriptomic references for scRNA-seq.

Ambient RNA. Every droplet carries some, and nuclei carry more: contamination metrics were universally higher for nuclei than for cells in controlled experiments arceneaux-2023. Uncorrected, ambient transcripts become differentially expressed genes and pathways: in dengue T cells all 17 significant GO terms before correction were driven by immunoglobulin genes arora-2025, and a published brain cell type (immature oligodendrocytes) turned out to be glial nuclei carrying neuronal ambient RNA caglayan-2022.

The upshot for salvage: before tuning QC thresholds, make sure the counts and the cell calls are not themselves discarding or inventing cells.

Standard practice

  • Quantification. Cell Ranger is the default for 10x data; STARsolo reproduces it much faster and is the engine inside the Human Cell Atlas pipeline Optimus; alevin-fry / simpleaf (via simpleaf) and kallisto | bustools (via kb-python) are the lightweight alternatives. Plate and custom protocols use zUMIs, scPipe or UMI-tools. Gene-ambiguous (multi-mapping) reads are discarded by Cell Ranger and by STARsolo unless --soloMultiMappers is set; alevin-fry resolves them by EM, and Optimus runs STARsolo with Uniform allocation.
  • Introns. Count them for nuclei (Cell Ranger include-introns, STARsolo GeneFull, alevin-fry splici or USA mode, kb nac). For cells the choice is open; the published comparison found it lowered agreement between workflows without improving clustering you-2021.
  • Cell calling. Pipelines ship a knee or order-of-magnitude rule (Knee / inflection-point cell calling), with Cell Ranger and STARsolo adding an EmptyDrops-style second step; the limits of that step are in the calling review (EmptyDrops).
  • Ambient RNA. SoupX, DecontX or CellBender, as covered in the calling review.

Benchmarked state of the art

Quantification. Five independent comparisons exist. None found a pipeline that changes biological conclusions on well-annotated human or mouse 10x data; the differences sit at the margins that salvage cares about (low-RNA barcodes, lowly expressed genes, non-model organisms).

  • You et al. compared 10 workflows on CEL-Seq2 and 10x mixtures with known labels. Almost every combination of workflow, normalisation and clustering recovered the labels; cells unique to a subset of workflows were under 5% of cells. zUMIs and scPipe recovered the most genes; kallisto bustools v0.39.3 was unsuitable for 6-bp UMIs; Cell Ranger was "consistently high and relatively stable" you-2021.
  • Brüning et al. found STARsolo, Cell Ranger 6, alevin and alevin-fry produced similar gene sets, and STARsolo, alevin and kallisto ran at least three times faster than Cell Ranger 6 bruning-2022.
  • Shainer and Stemmer (above) found kallisto ahead of Cell Ranger on gene detection in non-model organisms, with Cell Ranger calling more but lower-quality cells shainer-2021.
  • Du et al. found STAR detected more genes and agreed better with RNA-FISH than kallisto, at about 4x the time and 7.7x the memory du-2020.
  • Kuijpers et al. compared eight SPLiT-seq pipelines and recommended Parse's splitpipe or STARsolo, which gave nearly identical results; alevin-fry's splitp mode gave results the authors could not interpret kuijpers-2024.
  • In the alevin-fry paper (a competitor comparison, not a benchmark), a spliced-only kallisto|bustools index gave a mean relative false-positive expression of 0.328 per cell against 0.011 for alevin-fry with a splici reference and 0.001 for STARsolo alevin-fry / simpleaf. The kb nac index published since then addresses this but has not been independently re-tested kallisto | bustools.

On this evidence STARsolo is the benchmarked choice when Cell Ranger is too slow or not licensed for the chemistry, Cell Ranger is the stable default, and kallisto | bustools and alevin-fry / simpleaf trade a little specificity at low counts for speed and memory.

Ambient RNA, beyond the three benchmarks in the calling review.

  • Schroeder et al. (preprint) added a well-plate platform (BD Rhapsody) and a count-integrity test: how often a corrected count exceeds the raw count. CellBender and SoupX removed contamination reliably with minimal distortion. CellClear replaced more than 93% of counts with factorisation-derived values and did not scale to 172,000 nuclei, and scAR created cell types absent from the raw data (three coarse types in BD Rhapsody, up to eight in prefrontal cortex). DecontX and scCDC were the only tools usable without a raw droplet matrix schroeder-2026.
  • Meier et al. (preprint) tested the order of steps: doublet detection performed best before ambient correction, except with CellBender; running decontX first kept the largest share of doublets, because decontX and SoupX remove proportionally more "ambient" RNA from doublets meier-2026.
  • The three tools that the calling review mentioned only in passing now have records. FastCAR tied CellBender for the closest absolute contamination estimate in Nie et al., but tracked per-cell contamination poorly and ranked eighth of nine in Cargnelli et al. scCDC had moderate error and, like FastCAR, corrected mainly highly expressed genes. CellClear had the top subtype-level score in Nie et al. yet removed about as much endogenous as ambient RNA in Cargnelli et al. and rewrote the matrix in Schroeder et al.

Across the five ambient benchmarks, then, CellBender and SoupX are the most consistently recommended, DecontX is the safe choice without a raw matrix, and the aggressive tools (scAR, CellClear) need a count-integrity check before their output is trusted.

Cell calling. Still no independent benchmark of cell callers. The comparisons below are each made by one caller's authors.

Published but not independently benchmarked

Cell callers.

  • EmptyNN trains a positive-unlabelled neural network. Against hashing ground truth its AUROC was 94.73% against 79.87% for EmptyDrops, 86.88-90.16% for Cell Ranger v2 and v3, and 88.80% for CellBender; against genotype ground truth CellBender kept only 1,686 droplets where the others kept about 6,000 (AUROC 58.02%).
  • dropkick fits a per-sample logistic regression to confident cells and empties; specificity 0.9999 on high-background simulations against 0.9838 for EmptyDrops.
  • valiDrops combines adaptive metric thresholds, a cluster-marker test and a dead-cell classifier (median MCC at least 0.75 with as little as 0.1% dead cells). On a 10x 8k PBMC sample, most callers kept about 8,000 barcodes while dropkick and EmptyNN kept over 9,000.
  • DIEM targets nuclei: across six adipose samples 95.7% of its passing droplets were nuclear, against 87.9% for EmptyDrops and 84.5% for a quantile threshold, and EmptyDrops removed 1,038 and 782 nuclear droplets in two samples where DIEM removed 63 and 36.
  • SiftCell contrasts each barcode with shuffled counterparts; no numbers in its abstract.
  • QCatch (QCatch) adds cell calling and QC reports to alevin-fry output.
  • Read-level callers for pooled or combinatorial designs: ambimux estimates per-droplet ambient fractions while demultiplexing genotype-pooled multiome data and kept singlets correctly up to 60% ambient, against about 25% for ambient-unaware models; AmbientMapper does the same with multiple references for scifi-ATAC and rescues low-depth nuclei.

Ambient tools. AmbiDose (preprint) caps removal per cell and protects lineage genes; on a held-out human-mouse mixture it removed 92.0% of cross-species UMIs while keeping 99.6% of same-species UMIs. CellBouncer estimates, in pooled experiments, each donor's or species' contribution to the ambient pool. CLEANSER applies the same idea to CRISPR guides: a mixture model built on barnyard assays gives each gRNA-cell assignment a probability of being native rather than ambient, and its authors report that the choice of ambient filter changed differential expression results. Spike-in reference cells and DecontPro (tag counts) are covered elsewhere.

Quantification. cellCounts brings 10x quantification into R (Rsubread); UMI-tools remains the UMI deduplication engine of many custom pipelines; Optimised transcriptomic references for scRNA-seq rebuilds the annotation for droplet 3' data. Lightweight-mapping comparisons by the kallisto and alevin-fry authors (bioRxiv 10.1101/2021.01.25.428188 and 10.1101/2021.02.10.430656) are competitor comparisons and are not counted as benchmarks.

Wet-lab ambient reduction. In controlled inDrop experiments, cold protease dissociation, 0.1X DSP fixation, direct tip loading into the chip and about 1:1 dilution all lowered contamination metrics; 1% PFA fixation failed QC arceneaux-2023. See DSP reversible fixation for fixation in screen designs.

Nuclei, intronic reads and multimapping: signal or artefact

The calling review asks whether a barcode is damaged or just different. Upstream, the same question applies to reads.

  • Intronic reads in nuclei are signal. Most nuclear RNA is unspliced; dropping it shrinks libraries and blurs related types Counting intronic (nascent) reads, especially for nuclei. They also carry a gene-length bias, plausibly from internal priming in long introns, which matters when comparing genes, not cells (PMID 37257175).
  • Intronic reads in cells are mostly noise for clustering you-2021 but are what velocity and damage detection use: DropletQC calls damage from the unspliced fraction, so a pipeline that drops intronic reads removes the evidence the damage caller needs. Different tools split spliced, unspliced and ambiguous reads differently (distinguishing flanking k-mers versus splici and spliceu references; PMID 39657125), and that choice changes velocity results soneson-2021-velocity-preprocessing.
  • Multimapping reads are signal for some gene families. Discarding gene-ambiguous reads biases against paralogues and genes with low mappability; STARsolo and alevin-fry recover them by EM or uniform allocation STARsolo, alevin-fry / simpleaf. Pseudoalignment against a spliced-only index goes the other way and creates false-positive genes kallisto | bustools.
  • Ambient is higher in nuclei, and in high-ambient nuclei data a count threshold keeps debris that a profile-based caller removes DIEM, Knee / inflection-point cell calling.

Hypotheses and open questions

  • No independent benchmark of cell callers exists. The four caller papers above disagree on whether EmptyDrops, CellBender or their own method is best, and on the same 8k PBMC sample callers differed by about 1,000 barcodes. A ground-truth resource (hashing or genotype labels on empty and cell-containing droplets, as EmptyNN used) scored across callers would settle it.
  • Callers are tuned to one quantifier's UMI distribution; the 60,000-cell emptyDrops call on zUMIs and kallisto output you-2021 suggests that switching quantifier, or switching intronic counting on, silently changes calling. Not measured systematically.
  • Order of steps: if Meier et al. hold up, pipelines that correct ambient before calling doublets (with decontX or SoupX) are losing doublet calls meier-2026. Only a preprint so far.

Recommendations for low-cell multiplexed drug screens

Ranked by expected gain per unit of effort. Gains are from the cited settings, not from drug screens.

  1. Keep the raw matrix and the BAM. Every caller and the better ambient tools need the raw matrix, and damage and ambient demultiplexing need reads. Gain: keeps every later rescue possible. Data: raw-matrix, bam.
  2. Fix quantification before thresholds. Use Cell Ranger or STARsolo (Cell Ranger-like output, faster); count introns for nuclei Counting intronic (nascent) reads, especially for nuclei; enable multi-gene allocation if paralogous response genes matter. Use the same pipeline and version for every lane. Gain: up to 10% more cells per sample from the annotation alone bruning-2022. Data: fastq.
  3. Re-call cells with a profile-aware caller, not a knee. emptyDrops with a low floor, then check rescued barcodes with nuclear fraction and tag strength (calling review); for nuclei consider DIEM; treat EmptyNN, dropkick and valiDrops as second opinions, since none is independently benchmarked. Gain: self-reported only. Data: raw-matrix, tag-counts.
  4. Call doublets before ambient correction, then correct per lane. CellBender remove-background (order-independent), or SoupX or DecontX after doublet calling meier-2026. Avoid tools that rewrite the matrix (scAR, CellClear) unless a count-integrity check passes schroeder-2026. Gain: spurious ambient DEGs and pathways removed in arora-2025; doublets retained otherwise. Data: raw-matrix.
  5. At the bench: cold dissociation, reversible fixation and dilution lower ambient at the source arceneaux-2023; superloading with tags raises cells per lane (Superloading with sample multiplexing); its effect on ambient load has not been measured.

Chapter 12

Doublets, cell-cycle and stress signatures, batch and lane effects

61 records reviewed here, 76 records cited in the text

In this chapter

  1. Which of these three removes cells, and how much it costs
  2. Standard practice
  3. Benchmarked state of the art
  4. Published but not independently benchmarked
  5. Artefact or biology: how to tell
  6. Hypotheses and open questions
  7. Recommendations for low-cell multiplexed drug screens
  8. Records in this chapter

Scope: every RNA, ATAC and multiome doublet detector with real use, how independent benchmarks rank them, cell-cycle assignment and removal, dissociation and handling stress, and technical lane, plate and batch effects treated as QC questions (detection and diagnosis, not integration). The calling and damage review already covers scDblFinder, the Xi and Li and singletCode results, and the first dissociation-stress papers (scDblFinder, xi-li-2021, singletcode-2024, van-den-brink-2017, oflanagan-2019); this chapter adds the rest and does not repeat their numbers. Integration methods themselves are in the concept map (Harmony).

Which of these three removes cells, and how much it costs

Of the three topics, only doublet calling routinely deletes barcodes. Cell-cycle and stress handling usually change values rather than drop cells, and batch diagnostics delete nothing, but each can remove biology if used as a correction without a design that separates it from the effect of interest.

Doublets. Detectors are run at a removal rate, and the rate is usually the vendor rule of about 0.8% per 1,000 cells recovered Expected doublet rate from loading. In a hashed 20,000-cell lane that is about 16% of barcodes. Against hashing truth, the 10x rule underestimated multiplets, yet only 164 of 7,186 hashing multiplets (2.3%) were found by all eight tools tested, and the tools disagreed on which clusters held doublets: hashing put about 43% of its multiplets in one cluster where the tools found very few (PMID 41166377). So an RNA detector run at the expected rate removes a large set of barcodes that overlaps the true doublets only in part. More rounds of removal raise recall (two DoubletFinder rounds: recall +50%) by removing more barcodes Multi-round doublet removal. In the Demuxafy comparison, 0.4% to 78.8% of droplets were wrongly classified by the demultiplexers and detectors depending on method and pool size, and two detectors (DoubletDecon and DoubletFinder) misclassified noticeably more singlets than the rest Demuxafy, DoubletDecon, DoubletFinder.

Cell cycle. Regressing out phase scores is a default tutorial step Regressing out cell-cycle scores. It removes no cells but it removes every expression change correlated with the scores, which in a drug screen includes the arrest a drug causes cell-cycle-as-readout.

Stress. Handling time alone changed 1,185 genes in PBMC after 2 h at room temperature massoni-badosa-2020; filtering the stressed cells, as Gruffi does in organoids Gruffi, removes them outright, and dissociation choice can decide which disease-state cells survive at all dostalova-2026.

Keeping them safely means using orthogonal truth where it exists (tags, genotypes, receptor chains, read counts per locus in ATAC), choosing detectors by independent benchmark rather than by default, treating phase and stress as measured covariates that are reported per condition, and designing lanes and plates so that technical units are never confounded with condition.

Standard practice

  • Doublets. Python pipelines (scanpy) use Scrublet; the scverse and OSCA guides use scDblFinder; Seurat users commonly use DoubletFinder. All are run per capture lane at an expected rate Expected doublet rate from loading. Hashing and genotype pooling remove cross-sample doublets (Cell Hashing, Demuxafy). For scATAC, the ArchR workflow scores doublets by projecting synthetic doublets ArchR.
  • Cell cycle. Seurat CellCycleScoring and scanpy score_genes_cell_cycle score the Tirosh S and G2/M lists Seurat CellCycleScoring / scanpy score_genes_cell_cycle; OSCA uses scran's cyclone. Removal is by regressing the scores, or only their difference to keep cycling and non-cycling cells apart Regressing out cell-cycle scores.
  • Stress. Most pipelines do nothing by default. Common practice is to score a dissociation gene list and inspect it (van-den-brink-2017); at the bench, cold protease Cold-active protease dissociation or transcription inhibitors Transcription and translation inhibitors during dissociation, and cold storage of blood before processing massoni-badosa-2020.
  • Batch, lane and plate. Look at QC metrics per lane and plate and at each cluster's batch composition before integrating Per-batch QC distributions and per-cluster batch composition, scRNABatchQC. kBET and LISI are the usual numerical diagnostics and are among the scIB integration metrics kBET, LISI. When samples share a sequencing lane on patterned flow cells, DropletUtils swappedDrops removes swapped molecules swappedDrops (DropletUtils) barcode-swapping removal.

Benchmarked state of the art

RNA doublet detectors. Four independent studies score the same tools; together they say that the leading group is DoubletFinder, Scrublet, scds, Solo, DoubletDetection and scDblFinder, and that the order within it depends on data and metric.

  • Xi and Li (16 real datasets with annotated doublets, 112 simulated): DoubletFinder had the highest mean AUPRC (0.537) and Solo the highest mean AUROC; Solo and hybrid were the only methods that beat the library-size and gene-count baselines on every dataset, and doubletCells the only one that did not beat them on most. DoubletDetection and DoubletFinder most reliably restored the correct number of clusters; cxds was fastest and most resource-efficient; hybrid improved on both its components at little cost DoubletFinder, Solo, scds, DoubletDetection, doubletCells / computeDoubletDensity. A best mean AUPRC near 0.5 means that, averaged over thresholds, about half of the barcodes ranked as doublets were not annotated doublets.
  • Demuxafy (pooled PBMC and in silico pools of 2-128 donors): scds, scDblFinder and Scrublet were the top detectors by MCC and balanced accuracy; scDblFinder and Scrublet classified the most doublets correctly up to 16 donors and Solo did better than scds above that; DoubletDetection had the lowest share of wrong droplets (about 1-3%); Solo took a median 13 h per pool. Scrublet and scDblFinder were the most affected by added ambient RNA Demuxafy, Scrublet.
  • Ttoouli and Hoffmann (eight tools tuned per dataset against cell hashing): Scrublet most accurate by AUROC; after removal, DoubletDetection, scDblFinder and DoubletFinder gave the best clustering, ahead of removing the hashing multiplets alone Scrublet, DoubletDetection.
  • singletCode (lineage-barcoded singlets): weak performance for all four detectors tested (singletcode-2024); its ensemble test is the useful addition here.

Ensembles do not reliably beat their parts. Chord's own paper reports higher accuracy than its components, but Demuxafy's intersection of scds and DoubletFinder beat Chord in pools of 8 or more donors, and on singletCode data neither hybrid nor Chord always beat their components Chord. Combining a detector with tags or genotypes helps more than combining detectors: Demuxafy's recommended combinations pair one or two detectors with demultiplexing Demuxafy.

Cell-cycle assignment. One independent comparison exists. Guo and Chen ran Tricycle, Seurat scoring, Revelio and CS1CC on four small plate-based datasets with phases labelled by FUCCI or DNA staining. No method was consistently best; Tricycle was accurate on mouse and less so on human, matching its mouse reference; Seurat and Revelio assign every cell to a phase whether or not it is cycling; adding cells of known phase to the query improved every method guo-chen-2024, tricycle, Seurat CellCycleScoring / scanpy score_genes_cell_cycle, Revelio. Cyclone was not tested; the CycleMix authors report that both Seurat and cyclone perform poorly on droplet data and that Seurat labels mature neurons as cycling, a competitor comparison CycleMix, cyclone.

ATAC and multiome doublets, stress correction, batch metrics. No independent benchmark was found for any of these. Each tool below was evaluated only by its authors or by a competitor.

Published but not independently benchmarked

RNA doublets. vaeda (from the scds group) reports competitive scores on the 16 Xi and Li datasets and the best result among Python tools. SoCube, RADO (preprint) and Xoublet are newer detectors; Xoublet's own paper reports it is faster and lighter than Scrublet on 2.5 million cells but less discriminative on two of three benchmarks. ImageDoubler uses capture-site images on Fluidigm C1, up to 93.87% detection, and does not apply to droplets. Multi-round doublet removal is a strategy, not a tool.

Orthogonal doublet signals. Receptor chains and surface proteins mark doublets that expression cannot: over half of T cells with several TCR chains were doublets in standard and superloaded runs multi-tcr-doublets, and Double-jeopardy trains on such droplets to find more Double-jeopardy. In hashed data, a doublet can lose one of its labels and pass as a singlet; Nakaki and Sharpe model these partial-stealth multiplets and find them in real hashed and genotype-pooled data stealth-multiplets.

ATAC and multiome doublets. AMULET counts loci with more than two reads, which a diploid nucleus cannot produce, so it sees homotypic multiplets; on simulated PBMC multiplets its recall was 0.80-0.90 against 0.23-0.25 for ArchR, but on shallower islet data (below about 25K median reads) it fell to 0.35-0.37 and ArchR was better on one sample. scDblFinder's ATAC mode aggregates correlated peaks; its authors found AMULET good on one of three datasets and offer a combination of both (scDblFinder). scIBD targets heterotypic ATAC doublets. For multiome, COMPOSITE (17 DOGMA-seq datasets with hashing truth, 280,123 droplets), OmniDoublet and SEBULA (FDR-controlled, no synthetic doublets) combine modalities; each reports wins over the others' predecessors.

Continuous cell-cycle position and removal. peco (five genes, within 14% of the cycle in iPSCs), Cyclum, reCAT, CCPE, DeepCycle and VeloCycle (phase and speed from RNA velocity) give a position rather than a label. ccAFv2 (preprint) adds a neural G0 state and leaves uncertain cells unclassified; CycleMix can call cells non-cycling. For removal, ccRemover and scLVM remove only cell-cycle components, and CycleVI separates them into a latent subspace and reports better preservation of drug-response signal than score regression. ccRemover, scLVM and reCAT are no longer maintained.

Stress. Dissociation stress is conserved across tissues and present in published atlases machado-2021, strongest in brain myeloid cells, where enzymatic digestion creates an ex vivo activated microglia cluster that an inhibitor cocktail prevents Transcription and translation inhibitors during dissociation; 37 C enzymatic brain dissociation also changed neuronal and glial profiles against 4 C mechanical mattei-2020. Cold handling works for blood too: no global artefact after up to 48 h at 4 C massoni-badosa-2020. Computational rescue is partial: a sampling-time score flagged affected cells with AUC 0.888 and its regression helped mainly for delays under 8 h massoni-badosa-2020; tissue-specific stress panels removed 60-64% of the artefact against about 95% for the gentler protocol Stress-altered transcription gene panels; Gruffi removes stressed organoid cells Gruffi. The bench beats the computer.

Batch and lane diagnostics. CellMixS gives a per-cell mixing score that separates local batch bias from unbalanced composition. GTE (group technical effects) per-gene batch metric scores batch per gene and reports that as few as three highly batch-sensitive genes create a substantial batch effect, which suggests checking and excluding such genes before integrating. Silhouette-based batch scores are unreliable for this purpose rautenstrauch-2026. Index hopping is a lane-level artefact: a hopping probability of only 0.003-0.009 left more than 8% phantom molecules in over a quarter of samples and up to 85% in low-complexity samples, creating phantom cells PhantomPurgeR, swappedDrops (DropletUtils) barcode-swapping removal.

Artefact or biology: how to tell

Doublet or transitional state. A cluster that expresses two lineages' markers may be doublets or a real intermediate. Signals that separate them: doublets have about twice the UMIs of their parents (but so do large or G2/M cells), are enriched for cross-sample tags in hashed data, carry two receptor chains in lymphocytes multi-tcr-doublets, and in ATAC show loci with more than two reads AMULET. DoubletDecon's rescue step returns such clusters when they carry unique genes DoubletDecon; DoubletFinder's authors showed it left a validated hybrid kidney cell type alone DoubletFinder.

Homotypic doublets. Two cells of the same type look like one large cell. Expression-based detectors largely miss them (singletcode-2024); only tags, genotypes, receptor chains or ATAC read counts can see them. In a single-line screen this is most doublets.

Cycling or treated. G2/M cells have more RNA and can be mistaken for doublets by UMI caps. Phase fractions move with treatment, so a phase shift between conditions is a result, not a nuisance cell-cycle-as-readout. Check phase calls with two callers, since no caller is consistently best guo-chen-2024.

Handled or responding. The dissociation and handling signature (FOS, JUN, ATF3, heat-shock genes, NFKBIA) overlaps genuine stress responses to injury machado-2021 and, plausibly, to drugs. Only a control processed identically, in the same lane and at the same time, separates them handling-vs-drug-stress.

Batch or biology. A cluster made of one lane is an artefact only if lanes do not differ in condition. With plates confounded with groups, cell-level DE loses type I error control; summing per plate restores it but needs several plates per group lun-marioni-2017. Technical replicates of the same lines already vary substantially tung-2017, and confounded designs have produced spurious findings in published studies hicks-2018. kBET and LISI cannot tell a batch effect from batch-specific cell types without labels kBET, LISI.

Hypotheses and open questions

  • cell-cycle-as-readout: drugs that arrest cells change phase fractions; global regression removes that response. Report phase per condition and remove cell-cycle variation within condition or by disentangling. CycleVI's drug-response result is self-reported.
  • handling-vs-drug-stress: separate handling stress from drug-induced stress with vehicle wells handled in the same lane and time. Untested in screens.
  • Open: no independent benchmark of ATAC or multiome doublet callers, of stress-signature correction, or of batch-diagnostic metrics was found. Cell-cycle callers have one small independent comparison on plate-based cycling cells; none on droplet data, non-cycling cells or drug-treated cells. RNA detectors have not been benchmarked on drug-treated cells, where RNA content and state change with dose.

Recommendations for low-cell multiplexed drug screens

Ranked by expected gain per unit of effort. Gains are from the cited settings; none was measured in a drug screen.

  1. Let tags do the doublet work; use RNA detectors only for what tags cannot see. Remove cross-sample doublets by hashing or genotype first (Cell Hashing, Demuxafy), then run one leading detector per lane (Scrublet, scds, scDblFinder or DoubletFinder) where cell types are mixed. Gain: demultiplexing plus a detector beat detectors or ensembles alone in Demuxafy Demuxafy, Chord. Data: tag counts, filtered matrix.
  2. Do not delete at the vendor rate blindly. In a single cell line most within-sample doublets are homotypic and invisible to RNA scores singletcode-2024. Gain: avoids removing about 16% of a superloaded lane on a score that overlaps poorly with true doublets Expected doublet rate from loading. Data: filtered matrix.
  3. Design lanes and plates as blocks. Put every condition, including vehicle, in every lane or plate, so lane and plate effects are estimable and DE can be done per lane or plate in pseudobulk (lun-marioni-2017, Pseudobulk differential expression, scattered-vehicle-controls, Independent replicate wells or cultures per condition). Gain: restores type I error control under plate effects lun-marioni-2017. Data: replicates.
  4. Diagnose before integrating. QC metrics per lane, cluster composition per lane, kBET or LISI on vehicle cells only (where biology should match) Per-batch QC distributions and per-cluster batch composition, kBET, LISI; check for a few highly batch-sensitive genes GTE (group technical effects) per-gene batch metric. If several libraries share a sequencing lane on a patterned flow cell, run swappedDrops (DropletUtils) barcode-swapping removal. Gain: phantom molecules up to 85% in low-complexity samples PhantomPurgeR. Data: filtered matrix; molecule info or BAM for swapping.
  5. Keep cell cycle as a readout. Assign phase with two callers (for example tricycle and Seurat CellCycleScoring / scanpy score_genes_cell_cycle, or CycleMix where non-cycling cells are present), report phase fractions per drug and dose, and avoid global score regression before DE cell-cycle-as-readout, CycleVI. Gain: keeps arrest effects that regression removes; none measured. Data: filtered matrix.
  6. Prevent handling stress at the bench and measure the rest against vehicle. Fix or process all wells at the same time and temperature; for tissue, cold dissociation or inhibitors (Cold-active protease dissociation, Transcription and translation inhibitors during dissociation); for blood, 4 C until processing massoni-badosa-2020; fixation designs are in the design review (Methanol fixation, 10x Chromium Flex). Score the stress signature per condition and read only the excess over vehicle as response handling-vs-drug-stress. Gain: about 95% less artefact from the gentler protocol against 60-64% from computational panels Stress-altered transcription gene panels. Data: vehicle controls per lane.

Chapter 13

QC metrics, guides and modality-specific QC

32 records reviewed here, 42 records cited in the text

In this chapter

  1. What this chapter adds
  2. Standard practice
  3. Benchmarked state of the art
  4. Published but not independently benchmarked
  5. Modality-specific traps
  6. Hypotheses and open questions
  7. Recommendations for low-cell multiplexed drug screens
  8. Records in this chapter

Scope: the remaining QC-metric and threshold tools, damaged-cell detectors, best-practice guides, and QC for other modalities (CITE-seq protein tags, scATAC and multiome, single-nucleus RNA, spatial). The core argument about fixed versus adaptive thresholds, mito fraction as a damage marker, and the nuclear-fraction signal is made in the calling and QC review (MAD-based adaptive QC thresholds, miQC, ddqc, DropletQC) and is not repeated here. Doublet callers, including the ATAC-specific ones, are in the doublets review; cell calling and ambient RNA tools in the quantification and calling review.

What this chapter adds

Three findings change how QC should be read.

Most QC tools are reports, not models. Of the 182 tools that scRNA-tools files under quality control, few fit a model that decides which cells to drop; most compute the same metrics and draw them. The modelling tools are a short list: per-population mixtures (SampleQC, miQC), per-cluster thresholds (ddqc), supervised classifiers (cellity) and nuclear-fraction methods (DropletQC, QClus). The reporting tools (SCTK-QC, scRNABatchQC, scQCEA, QCatch, SingleCellMQC) are useful for one thing the modelling tools do not do: putting many samples, or many callers, side by side so that an outlier lane or a disagreement between callers is visible.

QC choices change biological counts by multiples. In one public snRNA-seq dataset of 33,600 intestinal nuclei, the fraction of gamma delta T cells ranged from 3.38% to 12.49% depending on calling strategy, and from 5.46% to 21.62% under strict filtering, a spread of about fourfold; within one QC stratum the call rate rose from 0.51% to 12.17% across deciles of genes per nucleus boloori-2026. The direction of error can also be the opposite of the salvage concern: re-analysis of six reference atlases with intronic fraction found organs where up to 85% of cells were nuclei-free, low-quality barcodes left in by the atlases' own QC montserrat-ayuso-2024.

Every modality has its own version of the same three metrics. Library size, complexity and a damage fraction reappear as fragment count, TSS enrichment and fraction in peaks for ATAC scATAC per-cell QC metrics, as total tags and isotype or background signal for protein, and as spot-level counts judged against neighbours for spatial data SpotSweeper. The same lesson carries over: global fixed thresholds confound biology with quality, and protocol differences move the metrics themselves de-rop-2024.

Standard practice

  • Guides. Three guides set most pipelines' defaults. The 2019 tutorial recommended judging counts, genes and mito jointly, keeping thresholds permissive and revisiting QC after clustering luecken-theis-2019. Its 2023 successor extends this across modalities and is the source of the widely copied 5-MAD rule heumos-2023. The Bioconductor book uses per-batch MAD outliers from scuttle and adds a check that discarded cells do not form a lost cell type, by comparing their average profile with the kept cells osca. The Hemberg-lab tutorial and course is the common teaching reference andrews-2021-tutorial.
  • Metric computation. scuttle::perCellQCMetrics and quickPerCellQC in R and scanpy.pp.calculate_qc_metrics in Python compute the same per-cell table; neither deserves a separate verdict beyond MAD-based adaptive QC thresholds. SCTK-QC runs EmptyDrops, several doublet callers and DecontX or SoupX in one pass and reports them together.
  • scATAC and multiome. Cells are filtered on unique fragments, TSS enrichment, fraction of fragments in peaks, nucleosome signal and blacklist fraction scATAC per-cell QC metrics, computed by ArchR (defaults TSS enrichment of at least 4 and at least 1,000 fragments), Signac or SnapATAC2.
  • CITE-seq. Protein tags are normalised per cell with CLR (Seurat's default) or with dsb, which uses empty droplets as the background. Cells are rarely filtered on protein alone; OSCA flags cells with outlying isotype-control or ambient-tag signal osca.
  • Spatial (sequencing-based). Spots are filtered with single-cell style thresholds by default; spatially aware alternatives are below.

Benchmarked state of the art

There is still no independent benchmark of RNA QC-thresholding tools beyond pipeComp, covered in the calling and QC review pipeComp. The independent comparisons found for this track are in other modalities.

  • scATAC feature engineering. Luo et al. compared eight configurations of five methods on scATAC and multiome data, after common ArchR-based QC. SnapATAC, SnapATAC2 and simple aggregation beat LSI-based methods; SnapATAC2 and ArchR scaled best SnapATAC2, ArchR. One result matters for QC: after dropping components correlated above 0.75 with library size, the Signac and ArchR embeddings were still correlated 0.5-0.75 with depth, against about 0.2 for SnapATAC2's cosine embedding Signac. In a design where conditions differ in fragment yield, depth can therefore drive clustering in LSI-based pipelines.
  • scATAC protocols. Eight scATAC methods in 47 PBMC experiments (169,000 profiles, one pipeline) differed in library complexity and tagmentation specificity, and these differences carried into annotation, genotype demultiplexing, peak calling, differential accessibility and motif enrichment de-rop-2024. TSS enrichment and fraction-in-peaks thresholds are therefore protocol-specific, not universal.
  • Spatial segmentation. Eleven segmentation methods across five imaging technologies and 15 datasets showed no single winner, and segmentation choice changed cell-type specificity, transcript contamination between neighbours and ligand-receptor results martinez-de-morentin-2026. Segmentation plays the role of cell calling in imaging data, and its errors look downstream like doublets and ambient RNA.

Published but not independently benchmarked

Multi-population and nuclei filters.

  • SampleQC fits a mixture model to QC metrics across groups of similar samples, giving each QC cell type its own component. In the authors' simulations the good cells that miQC and MAD rules wrongly excluded came almost entirely from one cell type, while SampleQC kept rare QC types; it ran on 867k brain nuclei from 172 samples.
  • QClus clusters nuclei on unspliced fraction, mito fraction and marker scores and removes empty and contaminated droplets. Against seven alternatives (Cell Ranger 7, CellBender, SampleQC, DIEM, DecontX, DropletQC, EmptyNN) on 252 heart samples and 1.9 million nuclei it scored best in the most samples, in the authors' own comparison. Its defaults are cardiac-specific.

Classifiers and coverage-based detectors. cellity trained a support vector machine on microscopy-labelled broken and empty Fluidigm C1 captures and reported over 30% higher accuracy than thresholds; it is the only QC method with imaging ground truth, but it has not been tested on droplet data. SkewC flags cells with skewed gene-body coverage, mainly useful for full-length protocols. SinQC (2016) flags cells whose expression is inconsistent with their quality metrics; no code repository was found.

Reports. scRNABatchQC and scQCEA compare many samples in one report, the latter adding a marker-based check that each library contains recognisable cell types. QCatch gives alevin-fry users cell calling and a QC report with splicing status. SingleCellMQC runs QC at sample, cell, feature and batch level across RNA, protein tags and immune receptors, with tissue-specific reference ranges.

Damage markers. MALAT1, a nuclear-retained RNA, tracks the spliced-to-unspliced ratio and can stand in for nuclear fraction when BAMs are unavailable MALAT1 as a cell-quality marker; the atlas re-analysis used it the same way montserrat-ayuso-2024. Both are consistent with scQCenrich, which includes MALAT1 among its features.

Protein tags (CITE-seq). ADTnorm aligns negative and positive peaks of each marker across samples and studies and scores staining quality; in its authors' comparison with 14 methods (CLR, dsb, DecontPro, totalVI, Harmony and others) on 13 datasets it aligned populations best. At the bench, titrating a 52-antibody panel raised median positive signal by 57% and lowered background from 26.3% to 14.9% of UMIs Buus et al. 2021 antibody titration for CITE-seq, so part of what ambient-tag tools such as dsb and DecontPro remove can be prevented before sequencing.

scATAC. scATAC-pro computes QC at each step for any protocol. Bin-based pipelines such as SnapATAC2 cannot compute fraction in peaks; Chromap peak-free scATAC QC (preprint) reports it at alignment without peak calling and found low-quality cells that SnapATAC2's QC missed.

Spatial. SpotSweeper judges each spot against its neighbourhood, so a biologically low-count region such as white matter is not removed wholesale, and found Visium spots that were low quality across many public datasets. SpatialArtifacts (preprint) finds contiguous artefacts such as dry patches and tissue lifting. SpotClean corrects spot swapping (bleed of UMIs between spots), the spatial analogue of ambient RNA; it needs at least 25% of spots off tissue. CyLinter removes cells affected by folds, debris and antibody aggregates in high-plex protein imaging.

Modality-specific traps

  • Single nuclei. Nuclei are nuclear by design, so the nuclear-fraction and MALAT1 signals that mark damaged cells in whole-cell data do not mark damage in nuclei; the relevant failure there is cytoplasmic or ambient contamination, which QClus and CellBender remove-background target. Mito reads in nuclei are contamination rather than a health signal. Rare-type counts in nuclei depend strongly on genes detected per nucleus boloori-2026.
  • Multiome. A barcode can pass on RNA and fail on ATAC or the reverse. Filtering on the intersection is the default; when one modality is the readout, filtering on the other modality's metrics alone removes cells for a failure that does not affect the readout.
  • ATAC depth. Fragment yield differs between protocols de-rop-2024 and leaks into LSI embeddings Signac, so per-condition fragment differences need checking before clustering.
  • Protein. Over-concentrated antibodies create background that looks like expression Buus et al. 2021 antibody titration for CITE-seq; staining batch effects need per-marker alignment rather than per-cell scaling ADTnorm.
  • Spatial. Global thresholds remove whole tissue regions with low counts; a local comparison SpotSweeper and artefact masks SpatialArtifacts separate the two.

Hypotheses and open questions

  • Open: no independent benchmark compares SampleQC, miQC, ddqc and nuclear-fraction methods on data with ground truth for damage. cellity's microscopy-labelled C1 data are the only such ground truth found, and they predate droplet platforms.
  • Open: the salvage literature argues for keeping more cells; the atlas re-analysis montserrat-ayuso-2024 argues that atlases keep too many. Both point to nuclear fraction as the deciding metric, which suggests the disagreement is about which metric to filter on, not about how strict to be.
  • Open: no method found sets ATAC or protein QC thresholds per condition. The condition-dependence argument made for RNA condition-aware-qc-audit applies equally to fragment counts and TSS enrichment if a drug changes chromatin accessibility globally.
  • Open: no independent benchmark of ADT normalisation was found; ADTnorm's 14-method comparison is the only multi-method one and is self-reported.

Recommendations for low-cell multiplexed drug screens

Ranked by expected gain per unit of effort. These add to the calling and QC review's list rather than repeating it.

  1. Report QC across lanes and conditions before filtering. Run a multi-sample report (scRNABatchQC, SCTK-QC or SingleCellMQC for CITE-seq designs) and look for a lane or condition that is an outlier on every metric. Gain: makes a failed lane or a condition-dependent shift visible; no measured number. Data: filtered matrix per lane.
  2. Model QC jointly across samples when cell types differ. Use SampleQC or per-cluster thresholds (ddqc) rather than one global MAD rule. Gain: fewer rare types excluded in simulation, self-reported SampleQC. Data: filtered matrix, several samples.
  3. Add a nuclear-fraction or MALAT1 check to whole-cell data. Flag cells with low intronic fraction (or low MALAT1) and low complexity as nuclei-free; do not apply the rule to nuclei. Gain: up to 85% low-quality cells in some atlas organs montserrat-ayuso-2024. Data: BAM or spliced/unspliced counts, or MALAT1 counts alone MALAT1 as a cell-quality marker.
  4. For CITE-seq readouts, titrate before the screen. Gain: 57% higher median positive signal and 43% less background Buus et al. 2021 antibody titration for CITE-seq. Then normalise with empty-droplet background (dsb) and align markers across plates or lanes (ADTnorm). Data: protein tags, raw matrix.
  5. For ATAC or multiome readouts, set thresholds per protocol and check depth by condition. Gain: avoids depth-driven clusters (LSI embeddings correlated 0.5-0.75 with depth Signac). Data: fragment files.

Chapter 20

Concept map: how QC choices reach the rest of the analysis

8 records cited in the text

In this chapter

  1. Concept map

QC is not a step that finishes before the analysis starts. Every choice made at cell calling, ambient removal, thresholding and doublet detection changes what normalisation, integration, clustering, differential expression, perturbation modelling, trajectories and multimodal analyses can see. This map draws those dependencies: the QC categories sit in the middle, the downstream concepts either side, and each line is one effect that a published study has shown or measured.

The concepts themselves are covered at a lighter depth than QC: a definition, the reviews and benchmarks worth reading, and a few anchor tools. Chapters 21 and 22 review them.

Concept map

QC categories in the middle; adjacent concepts either side. Point at a node to trace its links, select a concept to open its record. Each link is one evidence-backed effect, listed below.

Normalisation and variance-stabilising transformation

  • QC metrics & thresholds: Each cell's fraction of zeros falls as its total UMIs rise, and under log-CPM that fraction drives the first principal component in most datasets, so cells kept with very low counts can separate on depth rather than biology (Townes 2019, PMID 31870412)
  • Damaged & dying cells: Regressing out mito proportion or detected genes at the scaling step, instead of handling damaged cells at QC, nearly always increased correlation with those covariates and lowered clustering accuracy in pipeComp (PMID 32873325)
  • Batch, lane & plate effects: Per-cell normalisation does not remove batch: C1 technical replicates of the same iPSC lines differed substantially and their read-to-molecule conversion varied with technical factors (Tung 2017, PMID 28045081)
  • Cell calling: The shifted log applied to CPM (L = 1e6) performed poorly against size-factor-scaled counts, and on one dataset the benchmark first excluded cells with size factors outside 0.1-10x the median, so the size-factor range left by cell calling and QC is part of the input (Ahlmann-Eltze 2023, PMID 37037999)

Feature selection

  • QC metrics & thresholds: Selecting highly variable genes on log-CPM of cells with very different depths produced false variability in dimension reduction, which deviance on raw counts avoided (Townes 2019, PMID 31870412); deviance also gave the best gene ranking in pipeComp (PMID 32873325)
  • Cell cycle & stress signatures: Restricting integration to HVGs improved 74% of scIB comparisons but lowered cell-cycle and trajectory conservation relative to the full gene set, so HVG choice decides whether cycle and stress programmes survive (Luecken 2022, PMID 34949812)
  • Batch, lane & plate effects: Batch-aware variants of scanpy HVG selection gave no consistent advantage for integration over the standard variants across ten datasets (Zappia 2025, PMID 40082610)

Data integration and batch correction

  • QC metrics & thresholds: A single mito cut-off (5%) misclassified healthy and low-quality cells in 29.5% of human tissues (Osorio and Cai 2021, PMID 32840568), so a global threshold can leave batches with different cell-type composition, the harder non-identical-cell-types scenario of Tran 2020 (PMID 31948481)
  • Ambient RNA: Ambient load depends on sample preparation: neuronal ambient RNA was present in all glial types unless glia and neurons were separated before sequencing (Caglayan 2022, PMID 36240767), so contamination differs between batches and should be removed per sample before integrating
  • Cell cycle & stress signatures: scIB scores cell-cycle conservation explicitly; methods returning corrected expression (Scanorama gene output, ComBat, MNN) conserved cell-cycle variance best, while embedding methods and HVG restriction lost more of it (Luecken 2022, PMID 34949812)
  • Batch, lane & plate effects: The batch key chosen at QC (lane, plate, donor or study) defines what is removed; scIB found nested batch effects in atlas tasks and that scaling shifted every method toward batch removal at the cost of biology (Luecken 2022, PMID 34949812)

Clustering and cell-type annotation

  • Ambient RNA: Some previously annotated neuronal types in brain nuclei data were distinguished by ambient RNA, and the reported immature oligodendrocytes were glial nuclei contaminated with ambient RNA; after removal, rare committed OPCs appeared (Caglayan 2022, PMID 36240767)
  • Doublets & multiplets: Multiplets make up several percent of transcriptomes and confound downstream analysis (Scrublet, PMID 30954476); doublets of different types are likely misclassified, and distribution-based QC filters do not catch them (pipeComp, PMID 32873325)
  • QC metrics & thresholds: Stringent filtering on the whole population discarded subpopulations with extreme but healthy properties such as high library size, and clustering accuracy plateaued or fell as stringency rose (pipeComp, PMID 32873325)
  • Cell cycle & stress signatures: Enzymatic dissociation at 37 C induced immediate-early and heat-shock genes in subpopulations of cells (van den Brink 2017, PMID 28960196), and accounting for cell cycle revealed T-helper subpopulations that were otherwise undetectable (Buettner 2015, PMID 25599176)

Differential expression and differential abundance between conditions

  • Ambient RNA: Ambient RNA levels are highly sample-specific, and without correction DE between patients and controls called ambient transcripts as cell-type-specific disease genes (FastCAR, PMID 38030970; CellBender, PMID 37550580)
  • Doublets & multiplets: In simulations with doublets, removal by most detectors improved recovery of the true DE genes (Xi and Li 2021, PMID 33338399)
  • QC metrics & thresholds: A fixed mitochondrial cut removes viable malignant cells, whose high-mito share was twice the microenvironment's in 10-50% of tumour samples and tracked drug resistance, so condition-linked cells drop out before DE or abundance testing (PMID 40205439)
  • Statistics with few cells: Cells lost to QC lower cells per replicate; pseudobulk methods, which need replicates rather than cells, were all six top performers against matched bulk while cell-level tests called hundreds of false DE genes (Squair 2021, PMID 34584091)

Perturbation response estimation and prediction

  • Ambient RNA: Ambient gRNAs produce an excess of false-positive gRNA assignments in Perturb-seq, and the choice of ambient gRNA filter changed differential expression results (CLEANSER, PMID 39914388)
  • Damaged & dying cells: MIX-Seq found that navitoclax and AZD5591 gave strong selective viability effects but no robust transcriptional signature in captured cells, so the cells that die are missing from the response estimate (PMID 32855387)
  • QC metrics & thresholds: High mitochondrial fraction associated with higher IC50 across cancer cell lines, so a fixed mito cut can preferentially remove drug-resistant cells from treated conditions (PMID 40205439)
  • Cell cycle & stress signatures: Mixscape's local perturbation signatures, computed against nearest control cells, substantially reduced replicate, cell-cycle and stress variation, and 115 of 278 IFNGR2-guide cells were classed as escaping perturbation (PMID 33649593)
  • Hashing demultiplexing: In sci-Plex the number of cells recovered per hashed condition was a viability readout concordant with gold-standard measurements, so hash assignment and QC losses per dose are signal rather than noise (PMID 31806696)

Trajectory inference, pseudotime and RNA velocity

  • Doublets & multiplets: Heterotypic doublets created spurious branches in Slingshot trajectories on simulated data, which every detector except doubletCells removed (Xi and Li 2021, PMID 33338399)
  • Cell cycle & stress signatures: Accounting for cell-cycle variation revealed otherwise undetectable subpopulations corresponding to stages of naive T to Th2 differentiation (scLVM, PMID 25599176)
  • Alignment & quantification: The quantification pipeline sets the spliced and unspliced counts: five tools (13 approaches) gave substantially different abundances that changed velocities and interpretation (PMID 33428615), and only three of 22 splicing-based velocity methods were robust across alevin, dropEst, kallisto|bustools, STARsolo and velocyto outputs (PMID 42509564)

Multimodal single-cell data

  • Ambient RNA: Protein-specific ADT noise comes from unbound antibodies encapsulated in droplets and can be estimated from protein levels in empty droplets (dsb, PMID 35440536)
  • Cell calling: dsb's background correction needs the empty droplets, so the raw (unfiltered) barcode matrix must be kept past cell calling (PMID 35440536)
  • Doublets & multiplets: snATAC is too sparse for expression-style doublet simulation; AMULET counts regions with more than two reads and detects multiplets best from about 25K median valid reads per nucleus (PMID 34465366)
  • Hashing demultiplexing: Barcoded antibodies of the same kind as CITE-seq ADTs multiplex samples and flag cross-sample doublets, so hashing and protein panels share one library and one background problem (Cell Hashing, PMID 30567574)

Chapter 21

Preprocessing concepts: how QC choices reach normalisation, feature selection, integration and clustering

28 records reviewed here, 45 records cited in the text

In this chapter

  1. How QC choices propagate
  2. Normalisation
  3. Feature selection
  4. Integration and batch correction
  5. Clustering and annotation
  6. Records in this chapter

Part of the adjacent concept map. This chapter is lighter than the core chapters: one node per step, the standard tools and benchmarks for it, and the evidence for how a QC decision changes that step's result. Each concept record carries these as qc_links. The downstream steps (DE, perturbation, trajectories, multimodal) are in the downstream chapter.

How QC choices propagate

Normalisation, feature selection, integration and clustering run on whatever QC hands them, and none of them can tell an artefact from a cell. The evidence shows four routes.

  • Depth left in becomes structure. Under log-CPM, the fraction of zeros in each cell, which falls as total UMIs rise, drives the first principal component in most datasets scry deviance feature selection and GLM-PCA; technical cell-to-cell variation in zeros can be mistaken for biology (Hicks 2018, hicks-2018). Lenient cell calling keeps more low-count cells, so the normalisation and gene selection that follow must handle depth on counts, not on CPM (ahlmann-eltze-2023, Analytic Pearson residuals).
  • Covariates regressed out instead of handled at QC make things worse. In pipeComp, regressing out mito proportion or detected genes at the scaling step nearly always increased correlation with those covariates and lowered clustering accuracy pipeComp. Damaged cells are better handled at QC (MAD-based adaptive QC thresholds, DropletQC) than corrected afterwards.
  • Artefactual cells become clusters and labels. Ambient RNA defined some previously annotated neuronal types in brain nuclei, and the reported immature oligodendrocytes were glia contaminated with ambient RNA caglayan-2022. Multiplets are several percent of transcriptomes and confound downstream analysis Scrublet; distribution-based QC filters do not catch them pipeComp, so doublet detection (scDblFinder) has to happen before clustering.
  • Strict global thresholds remove biology before anything downstream sees it. Stringent whole-population filtering discarded subpopulations with extreme but healthy properties and did not improve clustering pipeComp; a 5% mito cut misclassified cells in 13 of 44 human tissues osorio-cai-2021. Integration then aligns batches whose composition QC has already changed.

Normalisation

Normalisation and variance-stabilising transformation. Size factors correct for each cell's capture and sequencing depth; a transformation then makes variance comparable across expression levels. The best independent evidence is ahlmann-eltze-2023: of 22 transformations, the shifted logarithm of size-factor-scaled counts followed by PCA did as well as or better than the rest, Pearson residuals did about as well, and the shifted log on CPM (1e6) did poorly. pipeComp rated sctransform best for separating subpopulations and removing library-size and detection-rate effects, with most other methods, scran pooled size factors included, fair pipeComp. Analytic Pearson residuals showed that sctransform's model reduces to an analytic Pearson residual and that UMI data are close to Poisson. A smaller benchmark of six methods ge-2025 put Dino first for 10x data and sctransform first for full-length protocols; it weighs less than the two above. Scaling every cell to the same total removes real differences in transcriptome size between cell types, often several-fold, so cross-type DE after CP10K reports size as expression ReDeconv and CLTS normalisation.

QC links. Depth and zeros (above). Do not regress out mito fraction as a substitute for QC. Per-cell normalisation does not remove batch: C1 technical replicates of the same iPSC lines differed substantially (Tung 2017, tung-2017). Reviews: Vallejos 2017 (PMID 28504683), Luecken and Theis 2019 luecken-theis-2019, Heumos 2023 heumos-2023.

Feature selection

Feature selection. Picking 2,000 to 4,000 genes whose variation exceeds technical expectation sets the PCA, the graph and integration. Deviance on raw counts gave the best gene ranking in pipeComp, with gains up to about 4,000 genes scry deviance feature selection and GLM-PCA. For integration and query mapping, zappia-2025 found Seurat-VST highly variable genes top-ranked across 24 methods and about 2,000 features sufficient. luecken-2022-scib found HVG selection improved 74% of integration comparisons.

QC links. Selecting HVGs on log-CPM of cells with very different depths produces false variability scry deviance feature selection and GLM-PCA. HVG restriction lowered cell-cycle and trajectory conservation relative to the full gene set luecken-2022-scib, so whether cycle and stress programmes (scLVM, van-den-brink-2017) survive depends on the gene list. Batch-aware scanpy HVG variants gave no consistent advantage zappia-2025. Reviews: Yang 2021 (PMID 34847932), Yip 2019 (PMID 29481632).

Integration and batch correction

Data integration and batch correction. Integration removes whatever is declared as batch while trying to keep identities and states. Two independent benchmarks disagree in a useful way. On simpler tasks, tran-2020 recommended Harmony, LIGER and Seurat anchor integration, Harmony first for speed. On atlas tasks, luecken-2022-scib ranked scANVI, Scanorama, scVI (scvi-tools) and scGen highest; MNN correction and fastMNN and Harmony were among the best on the immune task, and BBKNN corrects only the graph. Scaling pushed every method toward batch removal (79% of comparisons) at the cost of bio-conservation (72%).

QC links. The batch key chosen at QC (lane, plate, donor, study) defines what is removed. Ambient load depends on preparation: neuronal ambient RNA was in every glial type unless glia and neurons were separated before sequencing caglayan-2022, so ambient differs between batches and is best corrected per sample before integration (CellBender remove-background, DecontX, SoupX); this order is advice, not a tested result. Methods returning corrected expression (Scanorama gene output, MNN) conserved cell-cycle variance best luecken-2022-scib. A global threshold that removes a cell type in some tissues only osorio-cai-2021 leaves batches with different composition, the harder "non-identical cell types" case in tran-2020. Review: Argelaguet 2021 (PMID 33941931).

Clustering and annotation

Clustering and cell-type annotation. Graph clustering, usually Leiden community detection on a kNN graph, groups cells; annotation names them by markers, by classifiers trained on references (CellTypist, SingleR) or by mapping to an atlas (Azimuth reference mapping, scANVI in scvi-tools). In abdelaal-2019, a linear SVM was the best of 22 classifiers, SingleR was among the top five at deep annotation but slowest, and accuracy fell for overlapping classes and deep annotation levels. SC3 and Seurat led an earlier clustering benchmark (Duò 2018, PMID 30271584). CellTypist and Azimuth have no independent peer-reviewed benchmark yet.

QC links. Ambient RNA created and masked cell types caglayan-2022. Doublets confound clusters and markers, and removing them improved DE gene detection DoubletFinder. Strict thresholds remove subpopulations pipeComp. Dissociation induced immediate-early and heat-shock genes in subpopulations van-den-brink-2017, and accounting for cell cycle revealed otherwise hidden T-helper subpopulations scLVM. Reference annotators label every cell with a reference type, so damaged or doublet barcodes left in receive a confident-looking label unless a rejection option or mapping score is checked. Markers found by DE between clusters on the same cells that defined them have artificially low p-values (double dipping) TN test; ClusterDE repeats the clustering and DE on a matched one-population synthetic null to remove markers that over-clustering created. Distances and cluster sizes read off 2D UMAP or t-SNE are distorted chari-pachter-2023, so QC calls are better made in PCA space or on the metrics themselves. Reviews: Kiselev 2019 (PMID 30617341), Clarke 2021 (PMID 34031612).
